description: Beam-stack search is beam search that remembers what it pruned, so it is complete. Its *beam stack* holds one interval `[low, high)` of `f` values per layer, and the next layer admits only successors with `f` in that interval. When the search runs dry, it backtracks to the deepest layer that still has `f` values below the best solution cost `U`, moves that interval to `[high, U)` and builds the layer below again. It finds a first path as fast as beam search and reports each better one (it is *anytime*); when the stack is empty, the last path is optimal for an admissible heuristic. Memory stays at about `width` states per layer, but a narrow beam can take a long time to finish.

papers.title: Beam-Stack Search: Integrating Backtracking with Beam Search
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS 2005)
